660.name: RTC32SEL
660.title: External Oscillator Selection (32 kHz / 32.768 kHz)

The content of the internal compare output register is output on the corresponding T2CCx pins when a valid compare match occurs for a channel in compare mode 1 or concurrent compare mode. Note:A concurrent write operation to clear bit ENSHDW and set/clear bit(s) COOUTx is effective for initializing the internal compare output register. ENSHDW = 1: In this case, accessing bit COOUTx accesses the actual SFR bits. If COOUTx is set, the contents of register CCx will be transferred to corresponding channel x internal compare register. On set, COOUTx is held for one PCLK, then cleared automatically by hardware. Note:A concurrent write operation to set bit ENSHDW and bit(s) COOUTx (and clear bit TXOV) is effective for starting shadow transfer(s).

699.name: COOUT5
699.title: Compare Channel 5 Output
699.description: ENSHDW = 0: Any access to bit COOUTx accesses the corresponding bit of the internal 6-bit compare output register. Writing to bit COOUTx will change the corresponding bit of the internal compare output register. Reading from bit COOUTx returns the value of the bit in the internal compare output register. The content of the internal compare output register is output on the corresponding T2CCx pins when a valid compare match occurs for a channel in compare mode 1 or concurrent compare mode. Note:A concurrent write operation to clear bit ENSHDW and set/clear bit(s) COOUTx is effective for initializing the internal compare output register. ENSHDW = 1: In this case, accessing bit COOUTx accesses the actual SFR bits. If COOUTx is set, the contents of register CCx will be transferred to corresponding channel x internal compare register. On set, COOUTx is held for one PCLK, then cleared automatically by hardware. Note:A concurrent write operation to set bit ENSHDW and bit(s) COOUTx (and clear bit TXOV) is effective for starting shadow transfer(s).

699.name: TXOV
699.title: Enable Shadow Transfer On Timer Overflow
699.description: Set to enable for all compare channels, transfer of shadow value in T2CCU_CCx to the corresponding internal compare registers on overflow of their respective timer base.

699.name: ENSHDW
699.title: Enable Shadow Transfer With COOUTx
699.description: Clear to enable access of the internal compare output register via the COOUTx bits. Set to enable use of COOUTx bits for transfer of shadow value in T2CCU_CCx to the corresponding channel x internal compare register. Note:When setting bit TXOV, bit ENSHDW will be cleared by internal hardware. To ensure bit ENSHDW is set, user must ensure bit TXOV is cleared.

700.name: POLA
700.title: Compare Active Level for Channel Group A
700.description: In compare mode 0, the bit defines the active level of the outputs of the compare channels belonging to the group.

700.name: POLB
700.title: Compare Active Level for Channel Group B
700.description: In compare mode 0, the bit defines the active level of the outputs of the compare channels belonging to the group.

700.name: CM4F
700.title: Compare Channel 4 Interrupt Flag
700.description: Set on a compare match event on compare channel 4. This bit has to be cleared by software. Note:In case of software and hardware access to a flag bit at the same time, hardware will have higher priority.

700.name: CM5F
700.title: Compare Channel 5 Interrupt Flag
700.description: Set on a compare match event on compare channel 5. This bit has to be cleared by software. Note:In case of software and hardware access to a flag bit at the same time, hardware will have higher priority.

700.name: CCM4
700.title: Compare Enable for Channel 4
700.description: Note:Compare channels 4 and 5 should be enabled in a separate step after setting the compare mode via bits COMOD (and active level POLA/B if compare mode 0). This is to ensure defined compare output according to the selected mode on starting the respective compare channel. Note:The interrupt enable for compare channel 4 is controlled by the respective bit of SCU SFR MODIEN.CM4EN.

700.name: CCM5
700.title: Compare Enable for Channel 5
700.description: Note:Compare channels 4 and 5 should be enabled in a separate step after setting the compare mode via bits COMOD (and active level POLA/B if compare mode 0). This is to ensure defined compare output according to the selected mode on starting the respective compare channel. Note:The interrupt enable for compare channel 5 is controlled by the respective bit of SCU SFR MODIEN.CM5EN.

701.name: CCVALL
701.title: Capture/Compare Low Byte Value for Channel x
701.description: Capture: On read, CCVALL returns the low byte of the last captured value. Compare: CCVALL holds the low byte written. CCx acts as a shadow register to the channel x internal compare register. The value written is only transferred to the internal compare register when the corresponding bit T2CCU_COSHDW.COOUTx is being set (with ENSHDW = 1), or on overflow of the channel timer base. The read value always return the last written value.

702.name: CCVALL
702.title: Capture/Compare Low Byte Value for Channel x
702.description: Capture: On read, CCVALL returns the low byte of the last captured value. Compare: CCVALL holds the low byte written. CCx acts as a shadow register to the channel x internal compare register. The value written is only transferred to the internal compare register when the corresponding bit T2CCU_COSHDW.COOUTx is being set (with ENSHDW = 1), or on overflow of the channel timer base. The read value always return the last written value. Note:For T2CCU_CC4L/H and T2CCU_CC5L/H, only the compare function is available.

703.name: CCVALH
703.title: Capture/Compare High Byte Value for Channel x
703.description: Capture: On read, CCVALH returns the high byte of the last captured value. Compare: CCVALH holds the high byte written. CCx acts as a shadow register to the channel x internal compare register. The value written is only transferred to the internal compare register when the corresponding bit T2CCU_COSHDW.COOUTx is being set (with ENSHDW = 1), or on overflow of the channel timer base. The read value always return the last written value.

704.name: CCVALH
704.title: Capture/Compare High Byte Value for Channel x
704.description: Capture: On read, CCVALH returns the high byte of the last captured value. Compare: CCVALH holds the high byte written. CCx acts as a shadow register to the channel x internal compare register. The value written is only transferred to the internal compare register when the corresponding bit T2CCU_COSHDW.COOUTx is being set (with ENSHDW = 1), or on overflow of the channel timer base. The read value always return the last written value. Note:For T2CCU_CC4L/H and T2CCU_CC5L/H, only the compare function is available.

717.name: R
717.title: Baudrate Generator Run Control Bit
717.description: Note:BR_VALUE shall be written if, and only if, R = 0.

717.name: BRPRE
717.title: Prescaler Bit
717.description: Selects the input clock for fDIV, which is derived from the peripheral clock. others, Reserved

717.name: BRDIS
717.title: Baudrate Detection Disable
717.description: Note:It is recommended to toggle bit BRDIS after the reception of each LIN frame (complete or erroneous frame) to avoid a wrong Break field detection in noisy environments (i.e. spikes on the LIN bus).

717.name: BGSEL
717.title: Baudrate Select for Detection
717.description: For different values of BGSEL, the baud rate range for detection is defined by the following formula: fpclk/(2184*2^BGSEL) < baud rate range < fpclk/(74*2^BGSEL); where BGSEL = 00B, 01B, 10B, 11B. See table "BGSEL Bit Field Definition for Different Input Frequencies" for bit field BGSEL definition for different input frequencies.

718.name: BRK
718.title: Break Field Flag
718.description: This bit is set by hardware and can only be cleared by software.

718.name: EOFSYN
718.title: End of SYN Byte Interrupt Flag
718.description: This bit is set by hardware and can only be cleared by software.
enum: End of SYN Byte is not detected
End of SYN Byte is detected

718.name: ERRSYN
718.title: SYN Byte Error Interrupt Flag
718.description: This bit is set by hardware and can only be cleared by software.
enum: Error is not detected in SYN Byte
Error is detected in SYN Byte

718.name: SYNEN
718.title: End of SYN Byte and SYN Byte Error Interrupts Enable
enum: End of SYN Byte and SYN Byte Error Interrupts are not enabled
End of SYN Byte and SYN Byte Error Interrupts are enabled

719.name: FD_SEL
719.title: Fractional Divider Selection
719.description: Selects the fractional divider to be n/32, where n is the value of FD_SEL, and is in the range of 0 to 31. For example, writing 0001B to FD_SEL selects the fractional divider to be 1/32. Note:Fractional divider has no effect if the 11-bit BR_VALUE = 000H.

719.name: BR_VALUE
719.title: Baudrate Timer/Reload Value
719.description: The lower three bits of the 11-bit Baudrate Timer/Reload value. See also description in BGH register. Note:BR_VALUE shall be written if, and only if, BCON.R = 0.

720.name: BR_VALUE
720.title: Baudrate Timer/Reload Value
720.description: The upper 8 bits of the 11-bit Baudrate Timer/Reload value. When the 11-bit BR_VALUE is 000H, the baudrate timer is bypassed. Note:BR_VALUE shall be written if, and only if, BCON.R = 0.

725.name: BM
725.title: Data Width Selection
725.description: Note:The transfer and receive data width is maximum 8 bits. Transfer Data Width is 4...8 bits (<BM>+1). …
enum: Reserved. Do not use this combination.
Reserved. Do not use this combination.

725.name: PH
725.title: Clock Phase Control
enum: Shift transmit data on the leading clock edge, latch on trailing edge.
Latch receive data on leading clock edge, shift on trailing edge.

725.name: PO
725.title: Clock Polarity Control
enum: Idle clock line is low, leading clock edge is low-to-high transition.
Idle clock line is high, leading clock edge is high-to-low transition.

725.name: LB
725.title: Loop Back Control
725.description: This bit shall be set by software only in Master mode.
enum: Receive input is connected with transmit output (half-duplex mode)

726.name: MS
726.title: Master Select
726.description: This bit shall not be changed during operation mode.
enum: Slave Mode. Operate on shift clock received via SCLK.
Master Mode. Generate shift clock and output it via SCLK.

726.name: EN
726.title: Enable Bit = 0 (needed for programming mode)
726.description: Transmission and reception disabled. Access to control bits.

727.name: BC
727.title: Bit Count Field
727.description: This field is loaded with the programmed data width value (BM) when the SSC is enabled. It then counts down with every shift bit. Note:This bit field is not to be written to.

728.name: TE
728.title: Transmit Error Flag
enum: Transfer starts with the slave's transmit buffer not being updated

728.name: BE
728.title: Baudrate Error Flag
enum: More than factor 2 or 0.5 between slave's actual and expected baudrate

728.name: BSY
728.title: Busy Flag
728.description: Set while a transfer is in progress. Note: This bit is not to be written to.

728.name: RFF
728.title: Receive FIFO Buffer Full Flag
728.description: Note:FIFO full will be deleted as soon as the receive buffer is read by software.

728.name: MS
728.title: Master Select
728.description: This bit shall not be modified during operation mode.
enum: Slave Mode. Operate on shift clock received via SCLK.
Master Mode. Generate shift clock and output it via SCLK.

728.name: EN
728.title: Enable Bit = 1 (needed for operating mode)
728.description: Transmission and reception enabled. Access to status flags and M/S control.

729.name: BR_VALUE
729.title: Baud Rate Timer Reload Register Value, low byte
729.description: Represents the lower 8 bits of the 16-bit baudrate reload value.

730.name: BR_VALUE
730.title: Baud Rate Timer Reload Register Value, high byte
730.description: Represents the upper 8 bits of the 16-bit baudrate reload value.

731.name: TB_VALUE
731.title: Transmit Data Register Value
731.description: TB_VALUE is the data value to be transmitted. Unselected bits of TB_VALUE are ignored during transmission.

732.name: RB_VALUE
732.title: Receive Data Register Value
732.description: SSC_RBL contains the received data value RB_VALUE. Unselected bits of RB_VALUE will be not valid and should be ignored. Access point to FIFO. In case of FIFO overflow, the receive FIFO is blocked.

735.name: ADCENREQ
735.title: ADC Comparator Enable Request
735.description: This bit activates the ADC unit, the associated bandgap and clock required for the ADC unit. It is required to wait some time for the units to start after the request. In case ADCENREQ is cleared during ongoing conversion, then the ADC is disabled when the currently running conversion is ended.

735.name: ADCEN
735.title: ADC Comparator Enable Status
735.description: This bit indicates that the ADC unit, the associated bandgap, and the clock required for the ADC unit are active, and a subsequent conversion can be triggered. It is set after some time after ADCOMP_CON.ANCENREQ is set.

735.name: ADCIEN
735.title: ADC Comparator Interrupt Enable
735.description: Software can read this bit to get the status whether the interrupt is currently enabled or disabled.

735.name: ADCCHSEL
735.title: ADC Channel Select
735.description: This bitfield selects the channel and configures the 4:1 ADC multiplexer before a conversion is triggered. After a channel is selected, adequate time needs to be provided for sampling before a conversion is started.

735.name: VF
735.title: ADC Valid Flag for Result Register
735.description: Indicates a new result in ADCOMP_RES register.
enum: A new result is available in the ADCOMP_RES result register. The valid flag is automatically cleared when bit SOC is set.

735.name: EOCSAMPLE
735.title: ADC End of Conversion / Sampling Indication
735.description: This bit indicates that a conversion is completed and the result can be read. A new conversion via SOC can be started only when the EOC from the previous conversion has been set. This bit is automatically cleared when SOC is set.
enum: ADC conversion is currently going on
ADC conversion is completed. ADC is currently sampling.

735.name: SOC
735.title: ADC Start of Conversion Request
735.description: This bit activates a new conversion. Setting this bit has effect only when both, ADCEN and EOC, are set. This bit is automatically cleared by hardware once the conversion has started. If VF is set, setting SOC to 1 clears VF.

736.name: ADRES
736.title: ADC Conversion Result
736.description: This register shows the current converted ADC result. Software should ensure that the result is read before starting the next conversion. VIN = [LSB * (ADCRES-1)] ; LSB = 23.077 mV. Full Range : 5861.54 mV. For results of VIN =< 1, VIN is set to 0 V. Otherwise, VIN = [LSB * (ADCRES-1)].

738.name: WCAN_EN
738.title: WCAN Enable
738.description: This bit enables or disables the clock to WCAN Selective Wake-Up filter block.
enum: Disable Clock to WCAN Selective Wake-Up filter block
Enable Clock to WCAN Selective Wake-Up filter block

738.name: SELWK_EN
738.title: Selective Wake-Up Enable
738.description: The Selective Wake-up Enable function enables the protocol handler. The status of the protocol handler is also acknowledged through INTESTAT0.SWACK. The status of the Selective Wakeup Active is given in INTESTAT1.SWKSET. It also serves several functions when enabled. 1.Allows Wake-up source WUF to generate WUF_INT (see Figure "Wake- up Frame Detection"). 2.Allows error counter to generate ERROR_INT (see Figure "Error Counter"), indicated by INTESTAT0.ECOFL. 3.Triggers ERROR_INT and wake-up if there are any changes to the message object registers, indicated by INTESTAT0.MORC. 4.If a SYSERR occurs while SELWK_EN is enabled, then the Selective Wake-up function shall be disabled (ie., this bit field will be reset to 0). It is also indicated by INTESTAT0.ERSEL.

738.name: CCE
738.title: Configuration Change Enable
738.description: This bit field enables the configuration of the Bit Timing Registers. It also acts as soft-reset to the Selective Wake-up filter block. It has to be set back to '0' once the bit timing registers are modified for desired baudrate.
enum: The Bit Timing Registers (BTLn_CTRL), CDR Configuration registers (CDR_CTRL, CDR_UPPER_CTRL, CDR_LOWER_CTRL) and CAN_FD_CTRL may only be read. All attempts to modify them will be ignored.
The Bit Timing Registers and CDR Configuration registers may be read and written

739.name: CANTOMASK
739.title: CAN Time-Out Masking
739.description: This bit controls the interrupt masking for CANTO_INT interrupt.
enum: CAN Time-Out is masked - no interrupt is triggered
CAN Time-Out is signaled as an interrupt

739.name: ERRMASK
739.title: SYSERR Masking
739.description: This bit controls the interrupt masking for SYSERR interrupt.
enum: SYSERR is masked - no interrupt is triggered
SYSERR is signaled as an interrupt

739.name: WUFMASK
739.title: Wake-Up Frame Interrupt Masking
739.description: This bit controls the interrupt masking for WUF_INT interrupt.
enum: WUF_INT is masked - no interrupt is triggered
WUF_INT is signaled as an interrupt

739.name: WUPMASK
739.title: Wake-Up Pattern Detected Interrupt Masking
739.description: This bit controls the interrupt masking for WUP_INT interrupt.
enum: WUP_INT is masked - no interrupt is triggered
WUP_INT is signaled as an interrupt

740.name: SWACK
740.title: Selective Wake-Up Enable Acknowledge
740.description: This bit field indicates the acknowledgement of protocol handler enabled/disabled.
enum: Protocol Handler is disabled and configuration of WUF is possible
Protocol Handler is enabled and configuration of WUF should not be done

740.name: MODE
740.title: WCAN Mode of Operation
740.description: This bitfield indicates the WCAN mode of operation.

740.name: SYSERR
740.title: CAN Wake-Up System Error
740.description: The SYSERR indicates a configuration error (MORC), and an error counter overflow condition (ECOFL).
enum: System Error detected, WCAN enabling not possible. It also leads to SYSERR_INT interrupt trigger if enabled through ERRMASK.

740.name: CANTO
740.title: CAN Time-Out Detection
740.description: This bit indicates that there was an inactive CAN bus on RXDCO pin within tSILENCE of 750 ms. See section "CAN Message Timeout". A software write to INTESTATCLR0.CANTOCLR is required to reset this bit.
enum: CAN Time-Out detected. It also leads to CANTO_INT interrupt if enabled through CANTOMASK.

740.name: ECOFL
740.title: Error Counter Overflow
740.description: This bit field shows occurrence of Error Counter overflow. A set condition of this flag by hardware has higher priority than a clear through ECOFLCLR.

740.name: MORC
740.title: Message Object Register Changed
740.description: A set condition of this flag by hardware has higher priority than a clear through MORCCLR.
enum: Message object registers not modified after SELWK_EN is set
Message object registers was modified after SELWK_EN is set

740.name: ERSEL
740.title: Error Select
740.description: A set condition of this flag by hardware has higher priority than a clear through ERSELCLR.
enum: SYSERR is not set while SELWK_EN is enabled
SYSERR is set while SELWK_EN is enabled

740.name: WUP
740.title: Wake-Up Pattern Detected
740.description: This bit field is set when a falling edge on RXD (or WUP) is detected, when WCAN is in Standby mode. A software write to INTESTATCLR0.WUPCLR is required to clear this bit field.
enum: WUP detected. It also triggers WUP_INT interrupt when enabled through INTMRSLT.WUPMASK

741.name: WUF
741.title: Wake-Up Frame Detection (acc. ISO 11898-6)
741.description: This bit shows the status whether a Wake-up Frame has been detected.
enum: Wake-Up Frame detected. It also leads to WUF_INT interrupt trigger if enabled through WUFMASK.

741.name: SYNC
741.title: Synchronisation (at least one CAN frame without fail must have been
741.description: received) This bit is set when a valid Classical CAN frame is detected and is updatedafter every received Classical CAN frame. This flag is not updated when aCAN FD frame is received. Clearing this flag through SYNCCLR has higherpriority than a set condition by hardware.
enum: WCAN function not working or not synchronous to CAN bus
Valid CAN frame received, WCAN function is synchronous to CAN bus

741.name: CANSIL
741.title: CAN Bus Silent Time during Selective Wake Operation
741.description: This bit is set if there is no activity on RXDC0 pin on the CAN bus after tSILENCE of 750 ms expired. If any activity is detected on the bus, this bit is reset automatically. tSILENCE is fixed at 750 ms. This bit can also be cleared through bit WCAN_INTESCLR.CANSILCLR. A set condition of this bit has higher priority than a clear through CANSILCLR. 0BtSILENCE not exceeded 1BtSILENCE is exceeded

741.name: FDF
741.title: FD Frame Reception
741.description: This bit indicates reception of CAN FD frame. After reception of the CAN FD frame is completed, this bit is cleared to ‘0'.

741.name: RXDF
741.title: Filtered Receive Data Input
741.description: This bit shows the logic state of the filtered received data input signal (RXD_filt).

741.name: RXDS
741.title: Sampled Receive Data Input
741.description: This bit shows the logic state of the sampled received data input signal by the protocol handler.

742.name: ECNT
742.title: SWK CAN Frame Error Counter
742.description: If WCAN_FD_CTRL.FDEN = 0, the CAN Frame Error Counter is incremented when an error message or CAN FD frame is received, and decremented on a reception of a correct classical CAN frame, if ECNT>0. If FDEN = 1, the behaviour of the error counter is based on FDEC_DIS bit configuration. See section "Error Counter".

742.name: FDEC_DIS
742.title: Error Count Disable on CAN FD Frame
742.description: This bit is used to describe the behaviour of the Error Counter for FD frames. The value of this bit has no effect if WCAN_FD_CTRL.FDEN = 0. Note:When an FD frame is detected, the error is checked only until the FDF bit of the FD frame.
enum: Error counter is incremented or decremented based on correctness of the bitfields in arbitration phase of the FD frame
Error counter is active only for Classical CAN frames, and it is frozen for CAN FD frames

742.name: ECNTCLR
742.title: Error Counter Clear Bit
742.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the error counter FRMERRCNT.ECNT.

743.name: SYSERRCLR
743.title: CAN WUP System Error Clear Bit
743.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT0.SYSERR.

743.name: CANTOCLR
743.title: CAN Time-Out Detection Clear Bit
743.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT0.CANTO.

743.name: ECOFLCLR
743.title: Error Counter Overflow Clear Bit
743.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT0.ECOFL.

743.name: MORCCLR
743.title: Message Object Register Changed Clear Bit
743.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT0.MORC.

743.name: ERSELCLR
743.title: Error Select Clear Bit
743.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT0.ERSEL.

743.name: WUPCLR
743.title: WUP Clear Bit
743.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT0.WUP.

744.name: WUFCLR
744.title: Wake-up Frame Detection Flag Clear Bit
744.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT1.WUF.

744.name: SYNCCLR
744.title: Synchronisation (at least one can frame without fail must have been

744.name: CANSILCLR
744.title: CAN Silent Time during SWK Operation Clear Bit
744.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the corresponding status bit INTESTAT1.CANSIL.

756.name: TBIT
756.title: Number of Time Quanta in a Bit Time
756.description: This bitfield represents the number of time quanta in a bit time. The time quanta is based on fCAN frequency.

758.name: SP
758.title: Sample Point Position
758.description: Represents the sample point position. The sample point position is calculated as given in section "Filter and Sample Point Calculation". 33H represents the sample point position of 79.68 % (~80 %). The value shall be within 2CH to 38H (ie., 67.5 % to 87.5 %).

758.name: BRP
758.title: Baudrate Prescaler
758.description: This bitfield defines the scaling factor to derive one time-quanta.

760.name: CDREN
760.title: Enable CDR
enum: Disable CDR internal bit time measurement
Enable CDR internal bit time measurement

760.name: ESF
760.title: Error scaling factor
760.description: This bitfield defines the number of acquisition cycles on which average on error is calculated.

762.name: UPPER
762.title: CDR Upper Limit
762.description: This bitfield defines the upper limit for CDR internal bit time measurement. It should be configured as +5% of BTL1_CTRL value (integer part).

764.name: LOWER
764.title: CDR Lower Limit
764.description: This bitfield defines the lower limit for CDR internal bit time measurement. It should be configured as -5% of BTL1_CTRL value (integer part).

765.name: HIGH
765.title: CDR Internally Measured High Value
765.description: This bitfield shows the internally measured duration of a CAN bus bit as number of fCAN clock cycles (integer part).

766.name: LOW
766.title: CDR Internally Measured Low Value
766.description: This bitfield shows the internally measured duration of a CAN bus bit as number of fCAN clock cycles (fractional part).

768.name: FDEN
768.title: CAN FD Tolerant Enable
768.description: This bitfield enables or disables the CAN FD tolerant feature.

768.name: FDFILT
768.title: CAN FD Filter Time
768.description: This bitfield configures the filter time to detect the dominant bit field in FD phase. Refer to Table "CAN FD dominant bit filter time" for the FD filter time configuration for various baudrates. others, Reserved

769.name: DLC
769.title: Data Length Code
769.description: Valid values for the data length are 0 to 8. DLC > 8 will be considered as 8 data bytes, but the truncation will not be visible in this bitfield upon read.

770.name: ID
770.title: CAN Identifier
770.description: Identifier of a standard message (ID[28:18]) or an extended message (ID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits ID[17:0] are "don't care". This bitfield specifies ID7 to ID0.

771.name: ID
771.title: CAN Identifier
771.description: Identifier of a standard message (ID[28:18]) or an extended message (ID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits ID[17:0] are "don't care". This bitfield specifies ID15 to ID8.

772.name: ID
772.title: CAN Identifier
772.description: Identifier of a standard message (ID[28:18]) or an extended message (ID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits ID[17:0] are "don't care". This bitfield specifies ID23 to ID16.

773.name: ID
773.title: CAN Identifier
773.description: Identifier of a standard message (ID[28:18]) or an extended message (ID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits ID[17:0] are "don't care". This bitfield specifies ID28 to ID24.

774.name: MID
774.title: Mask for Message Identifier
774.description: Mask to filter incoming messages with standard identifiers (MID[28:18]) or extended identifiers (MID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits MID[17:0] are "don't care". If a specific bit in MID is set, the corresponding bit in the ID is considered for the ID matching evaluation, otherwise it is considered as "don't care". This bitfield specifies MID7 to MID0.

775.name: MID
775.title: Mask for Message Identifier
775.description: Mask to filter incoming messages with standard identifiers (MID[28:18]) or extended identifiers (MID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits MID[17:0] are "don't care". If a specific bit in MID is set, the corresponding bit in the ID is considered for the ID matching evaluation, otherwise it is considered as "don't care". This bitfield specifies MID15 to MID8.

776.name: MID
776.title: Mask for Message Identifier
776.description: Mask to filter incoming messages with standard identifiers (MID[28:18]) or extended identifiers (MID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits MID[17:0] are "don't care". If a specific bit in MID is set, the corresponding bit in the ID is considered for the ID matching evaluation, otherwise it is considered as "don't care". This bitfield specifies MID23 to MID16.

777.name: MID
777.title: Mask for Message Identifier
777.description: Mask to filter incoming messages with standard identifiers (MID[28:18]) or extended identifiers (MID[28:0]). For standard identifiers, bits MID[17:0] are "don't care". If a specific bit in MID is set, the corresponding bit in the ID is considered for the ID matching evaluation, otherwise it is considered as "don't care". This bitfield specifies MID28 to MID24.

778.name: DATA
778.title: CAN Data Byte
778.description: These bitfields specify the data bits 7 to 0 that will be compared with corresponding bits of (n+1) data byte of the received CAN frame.

779.name: PAGE
779.title: Page Bits
779.description: When written, the value indicates the new page address. When read, the value indicates the currently active page = addr[y:x+1].

779.name: STNR
779.title: Storage Number
779.description: This number indicates which storage bitfield is the target of the operation defined by bit OP. If OP = 10B, the contents of PAGE are saved in STx before being overwritten with the new value. If OP = 11B, the contents of PAGE are overwritten by the contents of STx. The value written to bitfield PAGE is ignored.

779.name: OP
779.title: Operation
enum: Manual page mode. The value of STNR is ignored and PAGE is directly written.
Manual page mode. The value of STNR is ignored and PAGE is directly written

New page programming with automatic page saving. The value written to the bit positions of PAGE is stored. In parallel, the former contents of PAGE are saved in the storage bit field STx indicated by STNR.
Automatic restore page action. The value written to the bit positions PAGE is ignored and instead, PAGE is overwritten by the contents of the storage bit field STx indicated by STNR.
